AI-MarkDone settings for Reader, export, formulas, and backup
item.description:
What this solves

AI-MarkDone has many actions, but you probably do not use all of them every day. Too many buttons can make the original ChatGPT page feel noisy.

item.title: ChatGPT Reader mode in AI-MarkDone
item.description:
What this solves

The ChatGPT page is good for continuing a conversation. It is not always good for reading one dense answer. Long paragraphs, formulas, tables, and code blocks can crowd the chat view.

item.title: Copy ChatGPT formulas as LaTeX, MathML, PNG, or SVG
item.description:
What this solves

Formula copy is easy to get wrong. You may need LaTeX for notes, MathML for Office, or an image asset for slides and documents.

item.title: Copy ChatGPT to Markdown with AI-MarkDone
item.description:
What this solves

ChatGPT’s built-in copy action is not always enough. You may want Markdown, but get citation noise, flattened tables, or formulas that need cleanup.

item.title: Directory note
item.description:
Current status

AI-MarkDone no longer exposes the standalone directory entry as a public feature. This page stays in place so older links do not break.

item.title: Dynamic annotations
item.description:
What this solves

When asking ChatGPT to revise a long answer, “make it better” is usually too vague. You often know the exact sentence or paragraph that needs work.

item.title: Export ChatGPT to Markdown, PDF, PNG, or ZIP
item.description:
What this solves

Some answers need to leave ChatGPT: notes, shared documents, archives, or images. Each destination needs a different format.

item.title: Install and refresh ChatGPT
item.description:
What this solves

AI-MarkDone is a browser extension, not a separate web app. After installation, it needs to load a content script inside ChatGPT before it can read the conversation and mount its controls.

item.title: Save ChatGPT answers with bookmarks and folders
item.description:
What this solves

Some answers are not ready to export immediately, but you know you will need them later. A browser bookmark saves the whole conversation, not the exact message.
